# Meta-Tagging Platform (prototype)

> A verbatim-grounded tag layer for academic literature. Rival definitions of a concept are
> scored against cases taken from what papers actually assert, every case anchored to an
> exact sentence in a paper. The corpus is a parameter the reader chooses, and the score
> changes with it - that is the finding, not a caveat.

Built by Shir Sivroni, The Open University of Israel.

## Read the data directly

You do not need to run JavaScript. Everything the site displays is recomputed in the
browser from these files, and they are served with `access-control-allow-origin: *`.

- [manifest.json](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/manifest.json): every file, every field, and its type. Start here.
- [papers.json](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/papers.json): the papers a corpus can be assembled from.
- [cases.json](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/cases.json): every case, with the verbatim quote it was read from and a P/N/U label.
- [definitions.json](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/definitions.json): the rival definitions, their gate verdicts and their published scores.
- [verdicts.json](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/verdicts.json): definition id to one character per case - '1' admits, '0' rejects, '-' not judged.
- [criteria.json](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/criteria.json): 14 candidate criteria for defining art, each with what it excludes. An OFFER, not a definition, and deliberately not scored - see below.

There is no separate endpoint for machines, and there will not be one: a parallel AI surface
drifts out of sync within weeks and then serves wrong numbers, which is worse than serving
none. The same files are offered as JSON Lines, written in the same build from the same
objects, for readers that prefer one self-contained record per line:

- [cases.jsonl](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/cases.jsonl)
- [definitions.jsonl](https://shir-openu.github.io/meta-tagging-platform-prototype/data/definitions.jsonl)

## How to reproduce any number

Choose a set of paper ids. Take every case from those papers whose status is P or N. For a
definition, compare its verdict character with the status ('1' against 'P' is a true
positive). Then

    MCC = (TP*TN - FP*FN) / sqrt((TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN))

The definition with id `circular` is a deliberate control: it copies the answer, so it must
score near +1.000 on any corpus. If it does not, the coding contradicts itself for that
corpus and no other number from it may be used.

## What you should not conclude

Single coder, so two-independent-coder reliability is not met and is not claimed. Confidence
intervals overlap at the top, so ranks are not separable. Scores are comparable only within
one run: instruction wording alone moves MCC by about 0.12 for an identical definition. The
corpus tilts contemporary, by choice.

## The criteria are an offer, and are not scored

`criteria.json` holds 14 candidate criteria for defining art, each with the cases it would
exclude. They are offered so a reader can keep the ones they accept, drop the ones they do
not, and add their own — a reader may decide one of the conditions is unnecessary and their
corpus may back them up. The interface composes the wording of whatever they keep. It does
NOT score it, and neither should you present a score for one: scoring means judging all 355
cases in the same run as the thirteen definitions, and a number from a separate run is not
comparable with anything on this site.

## Rights, and who a definition belongs to

The tag layer is CC BY 4.0. Paper text belongs to its authors and publishers; it is linked,
never redistributed. Quotes are short, for identification and verification.

Definitions drawn from the literature are attributed to whoever formulated them. Definitions
a person proposed carry `proposed_by` and `proposed_on` in `definitions.json`, and if you
quote or reuse one, use those. Not "a user": a one-sentence definition is too short and too
functional for copyright to attach, so the only thing that establishes ownership is
priority — a dated public record bearing a name — and an anonymous record establishes
nothing. Stripping the name off a definition when you pass it on is the specific harm those
two fields exist to prevent.

## Check your reading before you trust it

`reference_scorer.py` at the site root is a short, dependency-free implementation that
reproduces every published score from these files. Run

    python reference_scorer.py

and compare. It exists because an agent given only this URL reproduced the table but
reported that the recipe never said to SKIP cases whose verdict character is `-`. Read
naively, that single omission turns every number wrong: the circular control comes out
0.608 instead of 0.983.

## Two things here are NOT reproducible from these files, and we say so

- `lo` / `hi` come from a paper-clustered bootstrap (papers resampled, not cases, because
  cases from one paper are one author's usage). A case-level bootstrap will not match them.
- Seven of the scored papers have `url: null` — the pre-2010 classics — and they contribute
  98 of the 355 adjudicated cases. Their quotes were verified against stored text, but a
  third party cannot re-check those from this site alone.
